lines.t: Miss June walked downtown feelin' kinda low,
Cravin’ somethin’ sweet, didn’t know where to go.
Smelled cinnamon dreams floatin’ in the air,
A bakery popped up — hey, was that always there?
Bell on the door rang soft and clear,
Behind the counter stood a man sincere.
He smiled and said, “You look hungry, friend,
I’ve got Living Bread that’ll never end.”
He said, “Come on in, take what you need,
This ain’t your run‑of‑the‑mill kind of feed.
Fresh from Heaven, warm and true,
Baked with mercy and love for you.
No card, no cash, no paper price —
The Bread’s been paid for — my sacrifice.”
She blinked once, thought, “That’s kinda rare…”
But the smell of grace was everywhere.
She tried a roll, light as a cloud,
Said, “Mister, how’d you make bread that proud?”
He winked and said, “It’s the oldest art —
Started with love and a giving heart.”
She reached in her purse, said, “Let me pay,”
He shook his head, smiled, “Not today.
The cost was covered long ago, my dear,
Just take it home and keep Me near.”
He said, “Come on in, take what you need,
This ain’t your run‑of‑the‑mill kind of feed.
Fresh from Heaven, warm and true,
Baked with mercy and love for you.
No card, no cash, no paper price —
The Bread’s been paid for — my sacrifice.”
She laughed, said, “Sir, that’s mighty fair,”
And left with peace packaged up in there.
Turned ‘round once ‘bout halfway home,
That sweet bakery was gone — poof! all alone.
Just sunlight and street dust blowin’ free,
But the scent of grace stuck to her memory.
She whispered, “Lord, was that You in there?”
A dove flew by — she took that as a prayer.
Come on in, take what you need,
Taste the truth and you’ll be freed.
He’s got the bounty, fresh every day,
Bread of Life that won’t decay.
No lines, no bills, no earthly price —
He’s already paid, once and twice.
And if you smell Heaven in the air,
You might’ve found the Bakery That Wasn’t There.
